defects.title: depth --apply never populates the candidate table
defects.root_cause: write_depth_snapshot() only UPDATEs v4_exchange_pool_liquidity_snapshots; dex_candidate_pools is written solely by upsert_eligible_pool_rows(), reached only from refresh_pair()/refresh_key(), never from refresh_depth().
defects.why_fatal: The sizing path reads the CANDIDATE table (core/db/builders.py:688 and :823 -> balances: _json_loads(pool.get('balances_json'))), consumed by dex_quote_evidence_size.py:172 _liquidity_cap_raw(). A fully populated snapshot table has no effect.
defects.fix: New pool_manager/src/lib.rs::propagate_balances_to_candidate_pools() runs inside refresh_depth() when options.apply is set, UPDATEing dex_candidate_pools.balances_json from the snapshot via a correlated subquery. Rows without a measured snapshot are left untouched.

defects.title: candidate balances_json carries token addresses instead of amounts
defects.root_cause: upsert_eligible_pool_rows wrote "token0": pool.token0 / "token1": pool.token1, which come from v4_exchange_pools.token0/.token1 and are therefore 0x addresses.
defects.why_fatal: The consumer _pool_borrow_side_amount -> _positive_decimal_or_none -> _decimal RAISES ValueError('invalid decimal amount') for a 0x string instead of returning None; rust_closed_loop.py:3509 calls _liquidity_cap_raw() with no try/except, so the review loop would abort on an uncaught exception.
defects.latent_reason: The candidate balances_json was still {} before D5, so the exception was never reachable. Fixing propagation alone would have exposed it, so both must ship together.
defects.fix: token0/token1 now carry the measured snapshot amounts; the address identity moves to explicit token0Address/token1Address keys; with no measured snapshot the values are Value::Null so the sizing path degrades safely to its None fallback.

acceptance_criterion_correction.problem: The original criterion was checked against the SNAPSHOT table, but the sizing path reads the CANDIDATE table.
acceptance_criterion_correction.corrected: _liquidity_cap_raw() must return non-None when evaluated against the candidate table (dex_candidate_pools), which is the table the sizing path actually reads.
